audit.module_family_note: The PKS instantiation of this template. Four accepted types rather than one: a modular PKS gene normally carries a loading module of its own type alongside its elongation modules, and the cis-AT and trans-AT architectures are different enough that the strata below keep them apart rather than the selection rule. A gene is selected when every curated module type it carries is among these four, so a gene also carrying an NRPS module is excluded -- its architecture is drawn from two vocabularies.
audit.excluded_statuses_note: A retired entry is one MIBiG has withdrawn. Reconciling a computed architecture against an annotation its own curators have taken back would be auditing a retraction.
audit.model_panel_note: Declared, not discovered. Fixed at build time by scanning this corpus against the whole of the pinned Pfam release once, at the declared baseline cutoff, and listing every family that came back -- so it is a published vocabulary rather than a hint. It is a different panel from the NRPS instantiation's, discovered the same way, which is what an instantiation axis should produce: the method is shared and the vocabulary is the corpus's own.
audit.cutoffs_note: The three Pfam-curated cutoffs are per-model: the gathering threshold Pfam uses to define family membership, the trusted cutoff and the noise cutoff. The fourth is a bare E-value, which is NOT per-model and whose meaning depends on database size. The baseline is the gathering threshold; the others are R4 axes, and the measurement is that the three curated cutoffs are near-interchangeable on this corpus while the E-value is not.
audit.coordinate_spans_note: HMMER reports two spans per domain hit: the alignment span, which is the part actually aligned, and the envelope, which is the wider region the model is confident the domain lies within. Ordering an architecture by one or the other can reorder it, so the choice is declared and the alternative is measured. The baseline is the alignment span because it is the one a domain coordinate normally means.
audit.overlap_fraction_note: A hit is dropped when it overlaps an already-kept hit by more than this fraction of the SHORTER of the two spans. The shorter span is the denominator because a small domain nested inside a large one is the case the rule exists for, and measuring against the longer span would almost never trigger. The value is declared rather than swept: measured across 0.8 down to 0.0 the partition moves by at most a handful of genes, so a grid here would be four points reporting the same answer. What does move the answer is whether overlaps are resolved at all, and that IS an R4 axis.
audit.resolution_policies_note: Pfam resolves overlaps between families of the same clan by keeping the best-scoring hit. That rule is NOT available here: the pinned library carries no clan annotation at all, so this campaign's rule is score and geometry and is declared as its own rather than borrowed and misattributed. keep_all is the unresolved architecture -- the one the catalogued design assumed was already non-overlapping.
audit.domain_mappings_note: A Pfam family is not a domain type, and the ketosynthase makes the point harder than the adenylation domain does: Pfam splits it across THREE consecutive families, so counting all of them triples every module. The baseline takes the N-terminal family, which covers the catalytic core and occurs once per module. The mapping whose key is the declared secondary domain -- `at_domain` here -- is how that second reconciled type is counted, and it is not part of the R4 sweep, which varies the primary domain's mapping alone. The keying is checked at load time: if it drifts from the secondary domain's name the secondary reconciliation computes zero for every gene and nothing else complains, which is what happened once while this template was being generalised.
audit.curated_domain_keys_note: The typed domain blocks a MIBiG module can carry. Only their PRESENCE is used, never their coordinates: the campaign counts how many of these blocks carry a usable location and reports it at R1, because on this database almost none do and a campaign that silently worked around that would be hiding its own foundation.
audit.reconciled_domains_note: The two curated domain types this family reconciles. The primary one is the ketosynthase, which a cis-AT elongation module carries exactly once, so it is the count the curated record states most reliably and the one the mapping sweep varies. The secondary one is the acyltransferase, and it is where this instantiation earns its own design: a trans-AT module has NO acyltransferase -- the enzyme acts from a separate protein -- so the curated zero there is a claim rather than a silence, and the strata decide which it is.
audit.module_strata_note: The partition that makes this instantiation more than a relabelling. A cis-AT module encodes its own acyltransferase; a trans-AT module does not, and gets one from a separate protein. The annotation set records that distinction in the module type, so the stratum decides whether a curated count of zero acyltransferases is a silence or a claim -- and the campaign reads which from the per-module-type census rather than asserting it, so a release that started recording them would change the verdict rather than contradict a hardcoded fact. A gene whose modules span both strata is 'mixed'.
audit.module_pattern_note: A cis-AT elongation module's invariant core in Pfam terms: the ketosynthase as its three families, then the acyltransferase. Four families for two catalytic domains. The carrier protein is deliberately NOT in the pattern, because the optional reduction domains sit between the acyltransferase and the carrier -- measured, the five-family pattern that includes it matches a fifteenth as often. And note what the pattern cannot match: a trans-AT module has no acyltransferase, so the count is zero there by construction, which is the stratum showing through a second and independent measure.
audit.reconciliation_verdicts_note: Per gene, the computed count against the curated one. not_curated is a real outcome and not a gap: the record carries modules for the gene but names no domain block of that type, so there is nothing to disagree with.

pfam_a_hmm.note: 1.5 GB, so it is read from the pinned image rather than shipped. Pfam itself is CC0; the reason this file is not redistributed is size, not licence. This copy carries no clan annotation -- zero CL lines across all 19,632 models -- which is why the overlap rule here is score and geometry rather than Pfam's own intra-clan rule.
